title: Xanthe and the Salt Again
premise: Petra Montrose, a mercenary whose oath-god has gone silent, takes in a feral child who speaks the dead tongue of the salt courts beneath Thornfell. The child is Xanthe, a soul sold to the Undercourt by desperate parents, escaped and slowly unraveling. To save them, Petra must retrace her own buried past—she was born under the mountain, a tithe-child herself—and lead a ragged company of smugglers, apostate priests, and one repentant debt-collector down roads only she remembers. In the salt court, Petra discovers her silent god did not abandon her; it was devoured by the Underking, and its last ember lives in Xanthe. Petra offers her own inherited soul-debt in exchange, shattering the Underking's claim, and emerges into daylight with Xanthe as her heir—not of blood, but of choice.
about_author: N. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping disused mine shafts across three mountain ranges before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about debts, borders, and the people who live in the gaps between both.

chapters.title: The God Who Stopped Answering
chapters.summary: POV Petra. On a smuggling run through Thornfell, Petra prays to her oath-god Vessel-of-Salt out of habit and receives silence for the hundredth day. She completes the job anyway, hollow. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of a faith running on muscle memory.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Wrong Hour
chapters.summary: POV Petra. A mud-caked child appears at Petra's mountain door speaking a language no living kingdom uses, clutching a salt-white coin. When Petra touches the coin, old scars ache. Emotional beat: wary compassion wrestling with self-preservation.

chapters.title: Xanthe
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The child cannot or will not give a true name; Petra calls them Xanthe after the color of their eyes. Xanthe draws maps of tunnels that shouldn't exist—under Petra's own house. Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into unease.

chapters.title: What the Tithe Was For
chapters.summary: POV Petra. An apostate priest, Brother Ossian, translates fragments of Xanthe's speech: soul-tithe, court beneath, the price unpaid. Petra realizes her village's old customs were payments, and she was once on a ledger. Emotional beat: inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: The Debt-Collector at the Inn
chapters.summary: POV Petra. A courteous stranger named Marrow-Vane arrives asking after a runaway asset. Petra lies well, but he leaves a salt coin on the table—a summons. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Roads Only I Remember
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra decides to take Xanthe down rather than wait. She gathers her crew: smuggler Ferro, Ossian, and grudgingly Marrow-Vane, who defects claiming the Undercourt broke its own law first. Emotional beat: reluctant fellowship forged.

chapters.title: The First Gate
chapters.summary: POV Ferro. The company enters the abandoned Delve at Graywater. Xanthe navigates instinctively, singing snatches of the dead tongue that make the dark feel attentive. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by being watched.

chapters.title: Salt Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Ossian. They pass a flooded gallery where drowned tithe-children linger as echoes. One recognizes Petra's face and calls her by a childhood name: Sela. Emotional beat: identity cracking open like ice.

chapters.title: Marrow-Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Marrow-Vane. He admits he collected Xanthe's parents' souls when they defaulted; the child watched. He seeks not redemption but correction of an unlawful contract. Emotional beat: guilt without absolution, yet purpose.

chapters.title: The Silent God's Grave
chapters.summary: POV Petra. In a shrine-chamber they find Vessel-of-Salt's desecrated altar—the god didn't go silent, it was taken. Petra's oath-mark burns black. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into fury.

chapters.title: The Underking's Herald
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe (rendered through Ossian's translation). The herald offers terms: return willingly and your companions live. Xanthe almost goes—until Petra refuses to let duty be bought so cheaply. Emotional beat: love against duty, first collision.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weeping Stair
chapters.summary: POV Ferro. Ferro, secretly marked years ago by a debt of his own, sells their route to the court. The company scatters in an ambush of salt-formed soldiers. Emotional beat: betrayal as tragedy, not villainy.

chapters.title: Alone in the Deep Roads
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Separated from all but Xanthe, Petra navigates by half-remembered childhood senses she doesn't know she has. She begins to understand what she is. Emotional beat: terror becoming competence, becoming homecoming.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: POV Ossian. Captured with Marrow-Vane, Ossian reads the great ledger in the antechamber of the court and finds Petra's original entry: sold at age six, never collected. Emotional beat: horror at bureaucratic evil.

chapters.title: Audience with the Underking
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Dragged before the Underking, Petra learns the truth: her god's ember was swallowed whole, and it now burns inside Xanthe—the child is both hostage and vessel. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: The Price of a Soul, Itemized
chapters.summary: POV Marrow-Vane. The Underking offers Petra her old life, restored, if she surrenders Xanthe. Marrow-Vane testifies the contract was void—signed by a guardian, not the parents—buying the company time. Emotional beat: law turned into a weapon of mercy.

chapters.title: Ferro's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Ferro. Ferro returns, offering his own marked soul to void his betrayal and reopen the sealed gate. His sacrifice costs him his memories of the surface. Emotional beat: redemption paid in full, painfully.

chapters.title: Ember
chapters.summary: POV Petra. In the throne vault, Petra reaches into Xanthe and touches the god's ember—it recognizes her oath. She understands: the debt can be transferred to the one it was originally sworn upon. Herself. Emotional beat: love choosing the terrible thing.

chapters.title: The Unsigning
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Before the full court, Petra claims her own ledger-line and dissolves the contract with her blood and her god's ember, unmaking the Underking's legal claim to every tithe-soul at once. Emotional beat: climax—duty fulfilled by breaking the system that defined it.

chapters.title: Collapse of the Salt Court
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe/Ossian. With its contracts void, the court crumbles; freed souls stream upward. The company carries Xanthe, drained and flickering, toward the light as the mountain exhales. Emotional beat: exodus, exhaustion, hope.

chapters.title: Daylight Accounting
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Weeks later, at the rebuilt door in the mountain, Petra settles accounts: Ferro relearning bread and rain, Ossian writing a new liturgy, Marrow-Vane burning ledgers. Xanthe sleeps in sunlight, the ember dim but alive. Emotional beat: quiet repair.

chapters.title: Heir of Nothing, Heir of Everything
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra formally names Xanthe her heir—not of property, but of the reforged oath to a small, waking god. Together they walk the smuggler's road, upward. Emotional beat: identity chosen, love ratified, journey continuing.
